metaDescription: Free online Kubernetes Ingress generator. Build networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress from host, path and service lines with TLS and nginx annotations.
intro: Build a networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress from simple lines of host, path and service:port. Add ingress class, TLS, cert-manager issuer and common nginx annotations.
why:
Ingress manifests look simple but have many details: the v1 API needs a pathType and a backend with a named service and port, TLS needs the host list and a secret, and every controller uses its own annotations. Older examples online still use v1beta1, which no longer works.

Write one rule per line, such as app.example.com /api api:8080 Prefix, and the tool groups rules by host, adds the TLS section when you give a secret name, and sets the ingress class. For the nginx class it can add the SSL redirect, a body size limit and a rewrite target, and for cert-manager the cluster issuer annotation. Annotations differ between controllers, so check the ones you use. Your input is not uploaded.
howTo: Write one rule per line: host, path, service:port and optionally Prefix, Exact or ImplementationSpecific.
Enter the ingress name, namespace and ingressClassName.
Add a TLS secret name and cert-manager issuer if you want HTTPS.
Copy the YAML and apply it with kubectl.

faq.a: Prefix, Exact and ImplementationSpecific. If you leave the type off, Prefix is used. The path must start with a slash.
When you give a TLS secret name, all hosts in your rules are listed in one tls entry using that secret. With the cert-manager issuer set, cert-manager can create the certificate for you.

faq.q: Are the annotations valid for every controller?
faq.a: No. The nginx options only apply to the nginx ingress controller and are added only when the class is nginx. Other controllers use different annotations.

faq.q: Do I need a Service already?
faq.a: Yes. The Ingress points to Services by name and port. Create them first, for example with the Kubernetes Deployment Generator.
